rule_change.what: A silent lead-in of one full 16-frame block (0.64 s) now precedes the first narrated segment of every batch.
rule_change.why: Gate C canary defect. Call 6's rejoin-3 sat at batch offset 0.000 with narration starting on sample 0; LatentSync opened the mouth on frame 0 to match, and the delivered segment's first frame showed open lips with visible teeth.
rule_change.scope: Batch audio construction only. Narration, segment order, seed (20260820), guidance_scale (1), loop_mode (pingpong), the driving base and every approved master are UNCHANGED. The batch partition is byte-for-byte the same six calls with the same segments in the same order.
rule_change.effect: blocks +1 and submit +0.64 s per call, exactly, with no rounding interaction: ceil((c + 16/25) * 25/16) === ceil(c * 25/16) + 1. Cost +$0.0032 per call.
rule_change.evidence: The canary's four inter-segment gaps are 0.5 s (12.5 frames) of digital silence. Mouth activity there sits at the re-encode noise floor from 6 frames before onset through the onset frame, and all 28 frames inspected by eye across the four gaps show lips CLOSED, including the frame where audio begins. One block is 16 frames - more silence than the condition already proven to work - and it is the smallest lead-in that is structural rather than empirical, because the model provably works in 16-frame blocks (the canary returned exactly 145 x 16 = 2320 frames).

cost_summary.note: Six calls delivered 22 segments. call6_first_run_sunk_usd is the pre-lead-in canary; it bought the evidence for the boundary rule and is recorded as spend, not waste. Every call returned exactly its predicted 16-frame block count.

split_rule.what: Delivered segments are cut at the MIDPOINT of the surrounding silence: 0.240 s before the narration and 0.240 s after, instead of at the audio onset.
split_rule.why: LatentSync articulates before the sound. Call 4 measured ~6 frames of anticipation on Curtis - the mouth is open at return frame 913 while the first audible sample is at 919.3. Cutting at the onset lands inside that window, so a delivered first frame showed closed lips or open teeth depending on the segment first phoneme.

tail_margin_finding.what: The block rounding can leave almost no pad after the CLOSING segment of a batch: call 5 left 0.020 s and call 2 left 0.032 s, against the 0.240 s the cut rule wants.
tail_margin_finding.resolved_how: No re-run. Every Gate A master already carries 400-600 ms of its own trailing silence, which is the silence the mouth closes into. The tail is clamped to what the return offers and the real condition is asserted instead - at least 0.240 s of silence before the last delivered frame, counting the master internal trailing silence.
tail_margin_finding.planner_gap: plan-lipsync-batches.mjs still computes blocks from content alone. For the remaining catalog it should reserve the tail as well - blocks = ceil((content + 0.24) * 25 / 16) - so the closing segment always has pad.
